name: Jet peel (needle-free)
lead: A jet peel is an aesthetic skin procedure in which a handheld device propels a fine, pressurised stream of fluid or gas (commonly saline, oxygen or a serum) at the skin surface without needles. Clinics market it for hydration, a smoother appearance and as a way to deliver topical products.

Published evidence is very sparse. The only relevant record found is a small registered comparison of a hydrating treatment and a jet peel for facial skin hydration (23 participants, listed as completed in 2026), for which no results are available.[1] No peer-reviewed trial results on jet peel are summarised here.

paras: Jet peel devices use a high-velocity jet of liquid or gas to treat the skin surface, and providers describe the method as a needle-free way of applying serums, hydration or mild exfoliation. Proponents describe sessions as short and without downtime; these descriptions come from provider marketing rather than from the research reviewed here.

One trial registration, NCT07793149, compares a hydrating treatment branded KIRA with jet peel for facial skin hydration and skin rejuvenation in 23 participants; it began in May 2026 and is listed as completed, without published results.[1] No other studies were found.

refs.title: Comparison of KIRA Hydrating Treatment and Jet Peel for Facial Skin Hydration (NCT07793149)

card.summary: Needle-free pressurised-jet facial for hydration and product delivery, with almost nothing published behind it.
card.note: Only a small registered pilot comparison exists; no results published.

quick.overview:
A jet peel uses a pressurised stream of fluid or gas to treat or deliver products to the skin without needles. It is offered in clinics as a hydration or glow treatment.

The only related research found is a small registered comparison against another hydrating treatment, with no published results.
quick.mechanism: A handheld device propels a fine jet of saline, oxygen or serum at the skin surface; providers say this exfoliates lightly and drives products in.
quick.risks: No safety data specific to jet peel were found in the sources reviewed. Needle-free devices are generally described as low-downtime, but this has not been established by published trials.
